transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. You should leave the door and detergent drawer open between uses to allow air circulation and prevent mould growth. Run an empty hot wash with a washing machine cleaner or white vinegar to remove existing odours from the drum and seals. From what you have described, the most likely cause is musty/mouldy — biofilm hygiene (door seal, drawer, filter, drum). Next: Musty: wipe the door-seal folds, clean the drawer and the pump filter, run a hot 60-90C maintenance wash (empty) with a machine cleaner or soda crystals, and leave the door and drawer ajar between washes. Let me know what you find.
ok will give it a go. do i need to do anything with the door seal and drawer first, theres black stuff in both of them tbh

Yes, you should clean both the door seal and the detergent drawer to remove the visible black mould. This is a necessary first step before addressing any underlying drainage or ventilation issues causing the damp smell. Next: Drain smell: check the standpipe/U-bend/anti-siphon and the drain-hose installation and air gap (plumbing, not usually an appliance part). Let me know what you find.
ok, the sink/standpipe doesnt smell of drains at all, its just a damp musty smell from the drum and drawer. so is it the black stuff thats causing it? how do i clean the seal and drawer?

Yes, the mould in the door seal and detergent drawer is likely causing the damp smell. To clean them, remove the drawer and wash it with warm soapy water, then wipe the rubber seal thoroughly with a mixture of white vinegar or bleach and water. Next: Burning/electrical smell: stop using it and unplug it - treat as an electrical/mechanical fault, not hygiene. Let me know what you find.
ok thanks, will clean the seal and drawer then. do i just do the hot wash after that, and is it fine to use bleach or should i stick with vinegar?

You can run a hot wash cycle after cleaning the visible mould. It is generally safer to use white vinegar for routine maintenance rather than bleach, which can damage rubber seals over time. Is there visible black mould in the door-seal folds or drawer, and does it get worse after draining or when the machine has been shut up unused?

yes theres black spots and grey sludge in the bottom fold of the seal, and slimy black stuff in the softener bit of the drawer. not sure if its worse after draining tbh, i always shut the door straight after a wash so its prob shut up quite a lot
From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
